description: Multi-GPU DCGM monitoring using the exact supplied metric names. Flat-tariff GPU energy cost in EUR. Select one GPU UUID for detailed analysis.

panels.description: Joule-counter increase /3,600,000 for the selected time range. Counter resets are handled; missing samples can reduce coverage.
panels.title: Energy · range

panels.description: Measured GPU energy in kWh × the selected flat tariff. Excludes other host components and electrical losses.
panels.title: Cost · range

panels.description: One row per UUID. Current measurements use the end of the selected time range; range columns cover the full selected interval. Missing data stays blank. Counter totals require one logical scrape series per GPU. Exporter hostname may be a container ID. UUID identifies a physical GPU; GPU index is local to its host.
panels.title: Selected GPU · identity

panels.description: These are different activity measurements. DEV_MEMORY_UTIL_RATIO is kept separate from byte-derived VRAM allocation; a high ratio is not the fraction of memory capacity allocated.
panels.title: Compute and memory activity

panels.description: Fraction of cycles during which device memory sends or receives data. No inference about maximum achievable GB/s is made.
panels.title: DRAM-interface activity

panels.description: Separate byte gauges from the exporter. Used + free + reserved matches capacity in the supplied sample; asynchronous sampling can introduce small differences.
panels.title: Framebuffer · used, free and reserved

panels.description: Energy-counter rate in joules/second is watts. Compare with the instantaneous board-power gauge; different observation windows can produce differences.
panels.title: GPU power · two measurements

panels.description: Thermal trend only. Clocks dropping at high temperature can suggest throttling, but throttle-reason and power-limit metrics are required to confirm it.
panels.title: GPU temperature

panels.description: SM clock is already in hertz. Grafana scales the display to MHz/GHz; no extra multiplication is needed.
panels.title: SM clock

panels.description: Memory clock is already in hertz. It is not directly a memory-transfer bandwidth measurement.
panels.title: Memory clock

panels.description: The supplied PCIe metrics are gauges of bytes/s, including protocol headers. They must not be passed through rate().
panels.title: PCIe throughput

panels.description: Raw lifetime counter. Drops can indicate counter resets or a series change. Use increase() for selected-range retry totals.
panels.title: PCIe retry counter · raw

panels.description: Number of decreases observed within each raw series over a trailing window equal to the selected range. Driver-version or exporter-label changes create new series and are not counted as in-series resets.
panels.title: Counter resets · selected range

panels.description: Encoder and decoder activity ratios. These engines can remain idle during LLM inference.
panels.title: Video engines

panels.description: Raw exporter value only. No licensed/unlicensed mapping is assumed from the supplied HELP text. On a consumer GPU this can be irrelevant; a zero is not marked as a hardware fault.
panels.title: vGPU license status · raw code

panels.description: increase(joules_total[1h])/3,600,000 at each chart timestamp. The first points can include energy recorded before the dashboard start; this is a rolling window, not cumulative energy from the selected start.
panels.title: Energy · rolling 1 hour

panels.description: Rolling 1-hour measured GPU energy × selected EUR/kWh. A single flat price is applied retroactively to every timestamp.
panels.title: Cost · rolling 1 hour

panels.description: Raw joules since the driver counter was reset. This is not selected-range consumption. The range stats use counter-aware increase(), not subtraction of the endpoints.
panels.title: Energy counter · raw joules

panels.description: Board watts /1000 × EUR/kWh. This instantaneous cost rate can change with the workload and is not an accumulated bill.
panels.title: Electricity cost rate

list.description: Select a Prometheus-compatible data source, including Thanos configured as Prometheus.
list.label: Data source
list.name: datasource

list.description: Use one logical scrape path per physical GPU. Duplicate counter series will overcount energy and retries.
list.label: Exporter job
list.name: job

list.description: Prometheus target address. Useful when the exporter hostname is a container ID.
list.label: Scrape instance
list.name: instance

list.description: Uses the supplied hostname label; this can be a container ID rather than the physical host.
list.label: Exporter hostname
list.name: host

list.description: Filter by GPU model. Mixed models have different performance and thermal limits.
list.label: GPU model
list.name: model

list.description: Physical identity uses UUID, because the local GPU index can repeat on different hosts.
list.label: GPU UUID
list.name: gpu

list.description: Enter a non-negative number with a decimal point, e.g. 0.30. Flat EUR/kWh tariff applied to the entire displayed time range. GPU energy only.
list.label: Price (EUR/kWh)
list.name: kwh_price
